executive_summary: NASA named eight firms including Blue Origin, Lockheed Martin Space and SpaceX to Commercial Lunar Payload Services-2, a 10-year vehicle worth up to $10 billion for future lunar delivery task orders, and awarded six Venture-Class task orders worth approximately $1.3 billion to Arrow Science and Technology, Blue Origin and Impulse Space; both Rocket Lab-built ESCAPADE spacecraft completed powered Earth flybys on 7 and 9 November, and RKLB rose 6.5 percent at the last close. The read is that $10 billion is a ceiling on a competitive vehicle rather than money obligated, so value accrues to the few names already converting it into funded work such as the $94 million base contract to Blue Origin for the Promise rover, and I am wrong if task orders spread evenly across all eight named firms. Watch the Naval Sea Systems Command Super Intelligence presolicitation for a new attack submarine, responses due by 13 November: a strong industry response supports defence autonomy exposure, a thin one suggests the demand signal is rhetorical.
opportunity_of_the_day: Rocket Lab built both ESCAPADE spacecraft, which completed powered Earth flybys on 7 and 9 November, and RKLB rose 6.5 percent at the last close; the implication is that smallsat prime exposure is a direct way to own the NASA lunar and Mars award cycle, provided CLPS-2 task orders actually flow.
risk_of_the_day: Tehran said it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington ends the war, unfreezes assets and lifts oil sanctions, with Trump saying on 9 November the US was locked and loaded; the implication is that stalled Qatar and Pakistan mediation re-prices energy and defence names within days.

space.signal: These stories carry no dated near-term space catalyst, so the standing indicator is task orders actually competed under the $10 billion Commercial Lunar Payload Services-2 vehicle, for which no date is given.
space.watch: CLPS-2 lunar delivery task order awards
space.bull: Task orders flowing quickly to a narrow set of the eight named firms would convert ceiling into obligated work and support the lunar logistics names.
space.bear: A long gap between naming the eight firms and any obligated task order leaves the $10 billion as headline capacity only, with cash flow deferred.

defence.signal: The US House voted 211 to 204 to send impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the House Judiciary Committee, with any vote expected to be delayed until January.
defence.watch: Judiciary Committee handling of Hegseth articles, January
defence.bull: Continued leadership stability protects programme momentum such as the $2.37 billion fiscal 2027 Collaborative Combat Aircraft request and the 500 systems by 2032 target.
defence.bear: A live impeachment fight in January, when Democrats are projected to hold 256 House seats to Republicans 168, adds oversight drag to Pentagon procurement including the F-35 parts accounting the GAO called outdated, inaccurate, and incomplete.

geo.signal: Tehran set out conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz within two days, with Qatar and Pakistan leading mediation and Trump saying on 9 November there was positive momentum, though no date is given for any reopening.
geo.watch: Iran conditions for reopening Strait of Hormuz
geo.bull: Movement on the demands would ease the naval blockade in place since April 2026 and reduce the conflict premium around Gulf energy and shipping exposure.
geo.bear: No movement sustains the blockade that CENTCOM accounting links to more than $25 billion in lost Iranian crude revenue, and the land-route interdiction effort of Task Force Iron Gate widens the confrontation.

stocks.notable_movers: At their last close, defence primes LMT, RTX, NOC and LHX all posted moderate gains between roughly 1.7 percent and 2.5 percent, consistent with a market reading the Hegseth impeachment failure as continuity for current Pentagon posture, though ASTS fell sharply at nearly 8.7 percent and RKLB surged over 6.5 percent, signalling divergence between legacy defence beneficiaries and new-space plays. The RKLB move at its last close of $62.71 likely reflects momentum from its Q3 2026 earnings beat, while the ASTS decline at $33.69 suggests investors are reassessing the pace and cost of that programmes satellite broadband buildout.
stocks.sector_outlook: If the Hormuz diplomatic track produces a formal Iranian counter-proposal in the next 72 hours, counter-drone, escort and interceptor procurement demand signals across the Gulf will compress, shifting near-term opportunity toward longer-cycle land-based interdiction technology and away from maritime force-protection platforms.

stories.headline: NASA names firms to $10B lunar delivery contract
stories.context: NASA named Blue Origin, Firefly Aerospace, Intuitive Machines, ispace-US, Lockheed Martin Space, Northrop Grumman Space Systems, SpaceX and Voyager Technologies to its Commercial Lunar Payload Services-2 contract, a 10-year vehicle worth up to $10 billion, to compete for future lunar delivery task orders. NASA also awarded six task orders under its Venture-Class Acquisition of Dedicated and Rideshare launch services contract to Arrow Science and Technology, Blue Origin and Impulse Space, with a combined value of approximately $1.3 billion, to integrate and transport Moon Base cargo. Additional awards included a $94 million base contract to Blue Origin for delivering NASAs Promise rover to the Moon South Pole and miniCAST power and communications support contracts to Honeybee Robotics, Redwire and Yank Technologies.
stories.implication: Investors holding positions across multiple named primes gain broad lunar supply-chain optionality as NASA distributes Moon Base risk across eight competitors rather than consolidating it into one or two platforms.

stories.headline: ESCAPADE smallsats head to Mars after Earth flyby
stories.context: Both NASA ESCAPADE spacecraft, Blue and Gold, completed powered Earth flybys on 7 and 9 November, using the Oberth effect to slingshot toward Mars in what NASA described as the first use of a powered Earth flyby by a NASA spacecraft for a Mars trajectory. The two Rocket Lab-built smallsats launched the previous November aboard Blue Origins New Glenn and loitered near the Earth-sun L-2 Lagrange point before executing the manoeuvres. Both spacecraft are on trajectories to arrive at Mars two days apart in September 2027, where each will perform an 11-minute burn to enter orbit and study space weather.
stories.implication: The successful dual powered flyby validates Rocket Labs spacecraft bus capability for interplanetary missions and strengthens the case for smallsat-class science payloads on future national security deep-space applications.

stories.headline: Taiwan funds NT$71B space programme, eyes 2032 launch site
stories.context: President William Lai confirmed Taiwan has increased funding for the third phase of its National Space Technology Long-term Development Program to NT$71 billion, approximately US$2.16 billion, and extended the programme through 2031. A launch facility at Jioupeng in Pingtung County is expected to become operational in 2032, while a rocket research and assembly base at Shalun in Tainan is expected to begin operations in 2030. Taiwan currently relies on foreign launch service providers such as SpaceX to send its satellites into orbit.
stories.implication: Taiwans commitment to sovereign launch capability by 2032 opens a medium-term procurement window for ground infrastructure, range safety systems and smallsat bus suppliers willing to operate in a geopolitically sensitive programme.

stories.headline: Kratos signs offshore launch deal with Seagate Space
stories.context: Kratos Defense and Security Solutions announced a long-term agreement with Seagate Space for use of the companys Gateway offshore launch platform, with Kratos planning its first mission from the platform in 2027 and multiple additional launches anticipated in subsequent years. The announcement coincides with Seagate Space executing its first Gateway platform construction contract, moving the mobile sea-based launch infrastructure into physical construction. Kratos plans to use the platform initially in support of defense-related launch and target missions.
stories.implication: Mobile offshore launch capability entering construction in 2026 creates a new responsive-launch tier for classified national security payloads that need to avoid fixed land-range scheduling constraints.

stories.headline: US soldier arrested in Britain on Russia espionage suspicion
stories.context: A 41-year-old senior US soldier was arrested near Gloucester, in west England, on Tuesday on suspicion of offences under sections 1 and 3 of the National Security Act relating to obtaining or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence service, with British police stating the country to which the allegations relate is Russia. FBI Director Kash Patel described the case as involving allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies. The arrest came the day after at least ten Boeing KC-135R Stratotanker refuelling aircraft departed RAF Mildenhall, which the Wall Street Journal attributed to a threat from Iran, the second such apparent evacuation from British bases in three months.
stories.implication: The simultaneous exposure of a suspected insider espionage case and an Iranian-linked force protection evacuation from the same UK basing cluster signals compounding counterintelligence and force-protection risk for US forward-deployed air assets in Europe, with direct implications for operators planning rapid-tanker availability in a contingency.

stories.headline: House refers Hegseth impeachment articles to committee
stories.context: The US House voted 211 to 204 to send impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the House Judiciary Committee, effectively stalling the effort filed by Republican Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky. Massie charged Hegseth with negligence and illegal activity including attacking Iran without congressional approval, retaliating against a senator, and extrajudicial killings. Sending the articles to committee is expected to delay any vote until January, when Democrats are projected to hold the majority in Congress with 256 House seats to Republicans 168.
stories.implication: Hegseths survival until January preserves current Pentagon Iran war authorities for approximately seven more weeks, but the incoming Democratic majority with at least 256 House seats and 54 Senate seats makes a renewed impeachment drive in early 2027 the most significant near-term discontinuity risk for Gulf-deployed procurement programmes.

stories.headline: Iran Revolutionary Guards unit blamed for France supermarket cyberattack
stories.context: French authorities say Irans Revolutionary Guards Shahid Kaveh cyber unit hijacked refrigeration and freezer systems at approximately 700 French supermarkets in October, causing major food losses and around 20 fires, with investigators citing hackers use of Farsi and IP addresses pointing to machines in Iran. A judicial investigation targets the head of Shahid Kaveh and two deputies, and Irans ambassador was summoned, with Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot promising EU sanctions. Frances cyber crisis cell also links that unit and a second one to a 2023 cyberattack on the satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo.
stories.implication: The targeting of commercial cold-chain infrastructure at scale demonstrates that Iranian cyber operations have shifted from symbolic disruption toward economic attrition against allied civilian supply chains, widening the attack surface that critical infrastructure operators and their insurers must price.

stories.headline: CCA drones fly multi-ship formation in Air Force first
stories.context: The US Air Force achieved a milestone on 26 October when Shield AIs Hivemind autonomy software guided multiple Collaborative Combat Aircraft in a multi-ship formation executing beyond-visual-range counter-air tactics, though the number of aircraft and which specific CCA type participated were not stated in the company release. The Air Force has stated an intent to field 500 combat-ready semi-autonomous systems by 2032 with an overall fleet size of 1,000. The fiscal 2027 budget request included $996.5 million in CCA procurement funding, $150 million in advanced procurement for the following fiscal year, and $1.37 billion in continued research and development, for a total program request of $2.37 billion.
stories.implication: The formation-flight milestone accelerates the credibility of the $996.5 million fiscal 2027 CCA procurement request and strengthens Shield AIs Hivemind as a platform-agnostic autonomy layer with potential application across Leonardo Proteus and other allied uncrewed programmes already evaluating the same software.

stories.headline: GAO finds $2.5B in F-35 parts untracked by Pentagon
stories.context: The Government Accountability Office reported that as of March 2026 the F-35 programmes joint spare-parts pool comprised approximately 26 million parts valued at around $31 billion, of which roughly 17,000 parts worth up to $2.5 billion were not recorded in the Pentagons Enterprise Logistics Management System. The GAO described Pentagon records for F-35 parts as outdated, inaccurate, and incomplete and said minimal progress had been made since the problem was first identified seven years ago. In 2023, the GAO reported that one prime contractor lost more than 1 million F-35 spare parts worth more than $85 million from 2018 to 2022, and as of March 2026 the F-35 Joint Program Office still did not know the status of those items.
stories.implication: Persistent parts-accountability failures across a $31 billion inventory create readiness risk for the multinational F-35 fleet at the same moment operators are drawing on that pool at elevated operational tempo, and unresolved tracking gaps increase the probability of a mandatory programme audit that could delay near-term production deliveries.

stories.headline: Russia ships tanks and armoured vehicles to African ports
stories.context: C4ADS, a Washington-based organisation, identified a sample of twelve ships with operational ties to Russian military shipments carrying tanks, armoured vehicles and rocket launchers to African ports between 2023 and 2026, using AIS transponder data, satellite imagery and local reporting. The ports of Conakry in Guinea, Tobruk in Libya and Lome in Togo served as key logistics nodes, with five known military-affiliated transport ships tracked travelling from Russian Baltic and Arctic ports to Conakry between December 2024 and March 2026 for onward movement likely toward Mali. C4ADS also identified the port of Pointe-Noire in the Republic of Congo as a possible new logistics hub for Russian military operations in Africa.
stories.implication: Documented Russian arms logistics into West and North Africa via sea routes that bypass Western interdiction confirms the Africa Corps is consolidating a persistent land-force supply chain, increasing operational risk for European-backed security partners across the Sahel and creating demand for maritime domain awareness and vessel-tracking capabilities.

stories.headline: Iran urges US to meet Hormuz reopening demands
stories.context: Tehran said it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington meets conditions including ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US counter-blockade of Iranian ports. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Irans IRNA news agency that the only solution is diplomacy and addressing Irans demands, as Qatar and Pakistan lead mediation efforts following the conflict that began with US-Israeli strikes killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in late February. Trump said on 9 November there was positive momentum toward ending the conflict after meeting Qatars prime minister, while reiterating the US was locked and loaded but that further strikes were quite unlikely.
stories.implication: Until Hormuz reopens, global energy transit remains constrained and defence operators reliant on Gulf basing and maritime logistics face sustained operational pressure and elevated fuel costs.

stories.headline: CENTCOM stands up Task Force Iron Gate for Iran land routes
stories.context: US Central Command stood up Task Force Iron Gate, a team of approximately 20 civilian and military personnel based in Tampa, Florida, to block movement of advanced weapons, dual-use technologies and sanctioned materials across Irans land borders and the Caspian Sea, extending the naval blockade that has sealed Iranian ports since April 2026. The unit was created following a Reuters investigation finding Iran had imported approximately $2 billion in hardware, explosives and heavy trucks since January 2025 via Caspian Sea cargo ships, Central Asian trucking corridors and Chinese freight planes. CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper described the task force as complementing the existing naval campaign, while CENTCOM accounting puts Irans lost crude oil export revenue at more than $25 billion since the blockade began.
stories.implication: Analysts warn that a small intelligence-focused unit cannot seal Irans continental supply networks without regional cooperation and that disruption attempts risk drawing neighbouring states into the conflict.

stories.headline: Trump demands Israel and Gulf allies repay Iran war costs
stories.context: In a CBS News interview, President Trump said countries the US protected during the Iran war would pay back all war costs, explicitly naming Israel for the first time alongside Gulf states Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Bahrain and Kuwait that benefit from the US military presence around the Strait of Hormuz. Trump declared the war effectively over militarily while saying US forces remain locked and loaded if re-engagement is required, and said of Israel that without US intervention it would not exist. Analysts cited by Al Jazeera described the demand as political signalling rather than serious policy, with Gulf states expected to respond with quiet resistance given their existing contributions to regional security costs.
stories.implication: Repayment demands directed at Gulf states and Israel introduce a new financial and political variable for regional defence partnerships and basing arrangements that underpin US power projection in the theatre.

stories.headline: Fire contained at Irans South Pars gas field platform
stories.context: A fire broke out on a gas platform in Phase 14 of South Pars, a vital offshore natural gas field, and was extinguished quickly, according to Irans semi-official Fars news agency. Workers jumped into the sea and were subsequently confirmed safe aboard lifeboats and rescue craft after three heavy rescue vessels were sent to the platform, with Bushehr Province crisis management director Kourosh Dehghan confirming they were in good condition. Officials are considering a gas leak or operational mishap as possible causes, with the platform accounting for only 14.5 million cubic metres of South Pars total daily production of more than 700 million cubic metres.
stories.implication: Any damage to South Pars production capacity, even minor, matters to global LNG markets and to Qatar, which shares the reservoir as the North Dome field, and reinforces how Irans energy infrastructure remains vulnerable during the ongoing conflict.

stories.headline: US Navy seeks Super Intelligence for new attack submarine
stories.context: The Naval Sea Systems Command has an open presolicitation seeking industry concepts to use what it calls Super Intelligence to assist in designing a new attack submarine, with responses due by 13 November. NAVSEA plans to use an Other Transaction Authority mechanism in the coming stage and an approach to reduce technical risk before procuring the first platform. Requirements, schedule and the extent of artificial intelligence use remain unspecified in the notice.
stories.implication: Applying AI-assisted design to the SSN(X) programme signals that the Navy intends to compress submarine development timelines using autonomous design tools, creating early-mover opportunities for defence AI firms with naval engineering capability.

stories.headline: Leonardo targets autonomous ASW missions with Hivemind
stories.context: Leonardo is evaluating Shield AIs Hivemind autonomy software in the digital twin of its Proteus uncrewed helicopter at Yeovil, UK, with the goal of enabling fully autonomous anti-submarine warfare missions for the UK Royal Navy. An agreement between Leonardo and Shield AI was announced at the end of October 2026, intended to expand Leonardos ability to build its own mission autonomy software for the rotorcraft platform. The ultimate goal is to make Proteus a dominant anti-submarine warfare platform, according to a company spokesperson.
stories.implication: Integration of Hivemind into Proteus would position Shield AI as the autonomy layer for two separate major naval uncrewed platforms simultaneously, reinforcing the softwares competitive moat in allied ASW programmes.

stories.headline: Chinas GJ-11 stealth drone weapons bay revealed on CCTV
stories.context: Chinas PLA Air Force released footage on 9 November broadcast by state television CCTV showing the GJ-11 Xuanlong stealth uncrewed aerial vehicle, revealing its large internal weapons bay, upper-fuselage air intakes, flattened rear section, shielded exhaust nozzle and radar-absorbing coatings. The tailless, flying-wing aircraft was officially inducted into service in November 2025 and is claimed to have an estimated range of around 2,485 miles, capable of precision airstrikes, suppression of enemy air defenses and coordinated missions with crewed fighters. The footage also disclosed details of the drones live-fire strike mission and indicated a naval derivative, the GJ-21, reportedly conducted takeoff and landing operations aboard the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan in November 2026.
stories.implication: Publicising the GJ-11s internal weapons bay and stealth features signals that China is intentionally demonstrating a credible loyal-wingman and strike-ISR capability to adversaries, accelerating the operational calculus for US and allied CCA programmes.
